title: Ramified completed coefficient quotient comparison
statement: Let l be prime, E and L finite extensions of Q_l, and ι:E→L a Q_l-algebra embedding. Suppose e≥1, the ideal generated by ι(varpi_E) equals (varpi_L^e), index(e,n)+1=e(n+1), and j_n:O_E/(varpi_E^(n+1))→O_L/(varpi_L^(index(e,n)+1)) sends each residue of a to the residue of ι(a). For each scheme W there is a Coefficients datum of def-weil-ramified-pullback-tower-data: the completed inclusion, its same-index and ramified projection equations, the normalized scalar extension isomorphisms for coefficient modules, and their finite quotient transition equation. This is the coefficient part alone and asserts no pullback comparison or ramification existence.

source.place: Tags 093M and 03EK: quotient clause for completion and balanced tensor quotient; coefficient subargument of Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2(1), original node proof steps 2–4.

proof.text: Take the unique completed coefficient map of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison. Define the finite ring diagram using the literal quotient factor maps and identify its underlying ring-sheaf diagram with integralCoefficientSheafSystem by NatTrans.ofOpSequence. The limit equations then give projection_reduction for every pair a ≤ b. For n ≤ index(e,n), quotient induction and the specified formula for j_n identify the same-index inclusion with reduction to n followed by j_n. This proves the ramified projection square. The same quotient-induction calculation proves the transition square for the ramified maps for arbitrary a ≤ b.

Use the projection_surjective and uniformizer_kernel theorems proved inside lem-sp-completed-coefficient-regular-quotients. Apply the completed target constant-section ring homomorphism to the (n+1)st power of the given principal ideal equality. The constant-section compatibility of the completed inclusion and index(e,n)+1=e(n+1) identify the target projection kernel with the image ideal of the source projection kernel.

Prove the general sectionwise quotient base-change criterion directly. For a commuting ring-sheaf square R→S, R→A, S→B, A→B with sectionwise surjective quotient maps and ker(S→B)=c(ker(R→A))S, the tensor map sends s⊗a to q(s)j(a). Every tensor is s⊗1, since a lifts to R. The linear map v(s)=s⊗1 kills the image ideal of ker(R→A), by balancing. Thus a tensor killed by the displayed map is zero; surjectivity follows by lifting a B-section to S. These linear equivalences commute with restrictions. Sheafification and its counit give the normalized sheaf-module isomorphism. Transport along the fixed scalarWitness object equality to obtain coefficientIso and coefficient_formula.

Choose the isomorphisms just constructed together with their proved tensor formulas. Rewrite the coefficient_transitions goal by those formulas. Quotient transition maps preserve multiplication, their square with j was proved by representatives in step 1, and their composites with completed projections are projection_reduction. The two factors therefore agree. Package the completed map, its two projection equations, the coefficient isomorphisms, tensor formulas, and transition equations into Coefficients.

theorem coefficients_exists (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e)
    (hideal : Ideal.span ({integralScalarIntegerInclusion l E L ι
      (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)} :
        Set (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l L)) =
      Ideal.span {Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l L ^ e})
    (hexp : ∀ n : ℕ, index e n + 1 = e * (n + 1))
    (j : ∀ n : ℕ, Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1) →+*
      Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l L (index e n + 1))
    (hj : ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E),
      j n (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Padic.coefficientExtensionIdeal l E (n + 1)) a) =
        Ideal.Quotient.mk (Padic.coefficientExtensionIdeal l L (index e n + 1))
          (integralScalarIntegerInclusion l E L ι a)) (W : Scheme.{t}) :
    Nonempty (Coefficients l E L ι e j W)
